name: Congenital Complete Agenesis of Pericardium

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Agenesis of Pericardium

criteria.description: Definitive absence of pericardium confirmed by cardiac MRI or CT imaging
Electrocardiogram showing right axis deviation and poor R wave progression
Echocardiography demonstrating abnormal cardiac mobility and absence of pericardial echo window
Symptoms such as atypical chest pain or palpitations without other cardiac pathology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Definitive diagnosis requires imaging confirmation of pericardial absence by MRI or CT plus echocardiographic features; clinical and ECG findings support diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often incidental; imaging is essential to differentiate from other cardiac conditions.

imaging: Cardiac MRI demonstrating absence of pericardium and abnormal cardiac mobility
CT scan showing absence of pericardial tissue
Echocardiography revealing abnormal cardiac motion and absence of pericardial echo window
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Electrocardiogram with right axis deviation and poor R wave progression

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pericardial fluid on imaging
Pericardial thickening and calcification on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain with syncope
Signs of cardiac tamponade or hemodynamic instability
Evidence of cardiac torsion or strangulation on imaging
